The death of King James the Second at the Palace of St. Germains en l-aye, 1701. The persons standing by the bedside are T^ouis the Fourteenth, King of France, and the Cardinal dc Noailles, Archbishop of Paris; the youth kneeling is the Prince James Edward, afterwards called the Pretender; behind him is the Duke of Perth, his governor, whose right hand is pressed upon the clasped hands of the Duke of Berwick, as if endeavouring to allay the too audible expression of that nobleman's grief; on the left of the Duke of Berwick is the Earl of Middleton; the ecclesiastic kneeling in front is Father Sanders, King James's confessor; in the background are the bishop and his attendants retiring after the administration of the sacrament of extreme unction.

A hail storm in Petworth Park, October, 1832. Thedifterent manner in which the various animals then in sight were affected by the violence of the storm, gave great additional interest to the scene: the deer fled from it with tJie utmost rapidity to the shelter of a thick wood on the right; the sheep turned their heads from it, and most of them lay down ; the donkies also turned their heads from the storm, and drooping their ears, and crouching with their feet drawn as near together as possible, remained quite stationary during its whole continuance.
